issues.issue: This agreement is between EMC and Morgan Stanley Mortgage Capital Inc., a New York corporation, whereas the Section 1 definition of "Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement" in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement describes the May 1, 2007 agreement as being "between EMC and MSMCH" — Morgan Stanley Mortgage Capital Holdings LLC. Which Morgan Stanley entity gave the underlying warranties cannot be squared between the two.

"Accepted Servicing Practices" is defined by reference to "accepted mortgage servicing practices of prudent mortgage lending institutions," a circular and unmeasured standard, and the defined term is not used in any operative provision of this agreement. Its content and effect are both indeterminate.

"Appraised Value" is simply the value stated in an appraisal, with no lesser-of-appraisal-or-sales-price test, while the CLTV definition qualifies it as "the Appraised Value as determined pursuant to the Underwriting Guidelines" and the Loan-to-Value Ratio definition imposes a lesser-of test. The three cannot be applied consistently to the same property.

The Assignment of Mortgage must be both "in recordable form and in blank" and yet "sufficient ... to give record notice of the sale of the Mortgage to the Purchaser," requirements that pull against each other since a blank assignment names no assignee. Exhibit A-1(e) makes the choice depend on whether it is to be recorded, which this definition does not.

The Closing Date is May 31, 2007, one day before the June 1, 2007 Cut-off Date by reference to which Section 4 computes the Purchase Price and the Stated Principal Balance. A closing that precedes the balance measurement date cannot be worked through as written.

The denominator is "the Appraised Value as determined pursuant to the Underwriting Guidelines," but "Underwriting Guidelines" is a capitalized term that this agreement never defines. Whose guidelines determine the value, and therefore the ratio, is unstated.

"Covered" is fixed only by Appendix E of "Standard & Poor's Glossary," an undated external document that may be revised, so the category cannot be determined from the agreement itself. Which version of the Glossary governs is unspecified.

The Custodian is "the custodian specified on the Mortgage Loan Schedule attached as Exhibit B hereto," but Exhibit B as attached states only "Provided Upon Request" and contains no such designation. The identity of the Custodian, on whom Sections 5 and 6.03 depend, is not ascertainable from the instrument.

The Cut-off Date of June 1, 2007 falls after the May 31, 2007 Closing Date, although Section 4 fixes the Purchase Price by the Stated Principal Balance "after application of payments of principal due or received on or before the Cut-off Date." The two dates cannot be reconciled as a sequence.

The definition reads "repurchased or to be repurchase or replaced," a grammatical error that obscures whether a loan becomes a Deleted Mortgage Loan on repurchase, on becoming subject to repurchase, or on substitution. The trigger point matters for the substitution mechanics in Subsection 8.02.

The definition refers to "the FHA Regulations," a capitalized term never defined in this agreement. The circumstances in which the Commissioner or Secretary is included in "FHA" therefore rest on an undefined reference.

The definition of Co-op Loan breaks off mid-sentence ("secured by the pledge of stock allocated toa"), so the collateral it describes is incomplete on the face of the document. What qualifies as a Co-op Loan — which drives the Mortgage, Mortgaged Property and title-insurance provisions — cannot be read from the text.

"Fixed Rate Mortgage Loan" is defined as "a fixed rate mortgage loan purchased pursuant to this Agreement," a circular definition that supplies no criterion. Loans with fixed-then-adjusting rates are not addressed.

"FPD" is defined as first payment default provisions "as described in Subsection 8.03," but Subsection 8.03 describes no such provisions; it simply refers to the FPD provisions of the related Prior Purchase Agreements. The content of the defined term is located in documents outside this agreement.

The list runs "... NC Capital Corporation and Option One Mortgage Corporation, Option One Owner Trust 2001-1A, ...", so the conjunction placement leaves it unclear whether the Option One Owner Trusts are additional named sellers within Group 1 or a gloss on Option One. The group definition drives which loans get the Part A representations in Exhibit F.

The catch-all "or similar loan under any other applicable state, federal or local law" follows enumerated statutory labels, raising an ejusdem generis question about the reach of the residual. It is also unclear whether the assignee-liability qualifier limits every listed category or only the residual.

The date is that "specified in the related Mortgage Note and the Mortgage Loan Schedule," with no rule for the case in which the Note and the Schedule disagree. The Schedule itself is not attached, being "Provided Upon Request."

The Letter Agreement, which fixes the Purchase Price Percentage and is a required closing document under Section 10, is between Morgan Stanley & Co. Incorporated and Bear, Stearns & Co. Inc. — neither of them a party to this agreement. The price term therefore depends on a contract the contracting parties did not make.

The first sentence defines the Lifetime Rate Cap as a provision of the Mortgage Note, while the second imposes a substantive cap measured by "the amount per annum set forth on the Mortgage Loan Schedule," so the Note and the Schedule can produce different maximum rates. Which governs is not stated.

The denominator is the lesser of the Appraised Value and, "if the Mortgage Loan was made to finance the acquisition," the purchase price — leaving no second element for refinance loans — while the numerator uses the Cut-off Date balance even though the representations speak of the ratio "at origination." The ratio yields different answers depending on which reading is taken.

The MERS Procedure Manual is incorporated "as it may be amended, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time," so obligations measured by it can change without the parties' assent. The definition also uses a title ("MERS Procedures Manual") different from the term defined.

"Mortgage" is defined as the instrument "which creates a first lien on the Mortgaged Property," yet the agreement separately defines Second Lien Loan and Exhibit F warrants second liens on second lien loans. The definition cannot be given effect for the second-lien part of the pool.

The Mortgage File includes the Exhibit A-2 items "(to the extent in the possession of the applicable Servicer)," while Exhibit A-2 itself qualifies the same list "(to the extent in the possession of the applicable Seller)." Whose possession limits the delivery obligation cannot be determined from the two together.

"Mortgage Interest Rate Cap" (the limit on each adjustment) overlaps with the separately defined "Periodic Rate Cap," and the Qualified Substitute Mortgage Loan definition requires substitutes of the same type "with same Mortgage Interest Rate Caps." Which of the two defined caps must match is unresolved.

The Mortgage Loan Schedule is stated to be "attached as Exhibit B hereto," but Exhibit B as attached says only "Provided Upon Request," so the loan-by-loan data that the definition, the Custodian definition and Section 4's price calculation depend on is not in the instrument. What was actually agreed as the Schedule is left to extrinsic proof.
